method: Structured item-by-item re-classification of the 52 regex-flagged headlines, following a pre-written decision rulebook. Classifier: LLM-assisted (the assistant read each full headline and applied the rulebook below). This is NOT independent human annotation and is labeled as such in the paper; it serves as an internal audit of the regex classifier.

rulebook.step1_P: Does the headline state or clearly imply that the company's stock price has ALREADY moved (past/present-perfect tense, e.g. 'dropped 5% after earnings', 'soars after results', 'has gained 5% so far', 'second-best day ever', 'falls below 200-day SMA')? Includes realized moves stated together with a fundamental cause. -> P (realized price move)
rulebook.step2_E: Else: is the matched keyword part of a FUNDAMENTAL result or event magnitude (e.g. 'revenue rises 12%', 'sales jump', 'FQ1 gains' expected from earnings) or an analyst catalyst action, with NO realized stock-price move? -> E (fundamental magnitude/event)
rulebook.step3_D: Else: is the keyword a FORECAST or expectation of future stock direction ('could sink', 'may drop to $300', 'can it bounce back')? -> D (directional expectation only)
rulebook.step4_N: Else: the keyword is incidental with no stock-price meaning ('execution short fall' = shortfall; 'dropped October deals' = retail promotions released). -> N (regex false positive)
rulebook.tie_rule: When a headline contains both a realized stock move and a fundamental result (e.g. 'shares jump on blowout results'), classify P: the defining feature of an echo headline is that the realized move is reported.

notes.44: 'execution short fall' = shortfall, not a stock fall. Regex matched 'fall'.
notes.47: 'just dropped October deals' = released retail promotions, not a stock move.
notes.48: 'Dropping a Huge Deal Event' = releasing a sale, not a stock move.
notes.17: 'revenue rises 12%' - rise refers to revenue, not the stock.
notes.49: 'Sales rise 11.2%' - rise refers to sales, not the stock.
notes.18: 'FQ1 gains' = expected earnings gains; analyst catalyst watch, no realized move.
notes.7: Earnings preview asking whether stock 'can bounce back' - pre-event expectation.
notes.32: 'options surge on selloff day' - surge is options volume, but the selloff (realized stock move) is stated; classified P.
notes.31: dual content: 'Sales Jump' (fundamental) AND 'Stock Suffers Worst Day' (realized); P by tie rule.
